references.text: The Lord commanded Israel to turn toward the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea, which is the same command mentioned in Deuteronomy 2:1.
Describes the journey around the land of Edom via the Red Sea, corresponding to the wandering around Mount Seir.
Part of the travel account that includes the areas near Mount Seir and Edom.
The Lord's command to turn and head toward the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea, which directly leads to the event in Deuteronomy 2:1.
Refers to the way toward the Red Sea (Yam Suf) that Israel followed.
Jephthah summarizes Israel's journey around Edom and Moab, including the time they spent near Mount Seir.
Esau settled in Mount Seir, which explains why Israel had to wander around this area.
